beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: On Arua, hesitation before fleeing is diagnosed as a defect.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those Who No Longer Run asks what happens when safety needs that defect.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This science fiction novel makes fear a foundation of political order.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its question reaches beyond whether one unusual young man can be brave.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Who decides which bodies belong inside a peaceful society?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And what changes when the exception becomes useful to power?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The story invites you to examine protection through one family's life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Arua turns one face toward its star, leaving the other in darkness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Life occupies a narrow Twilight Belt between lethal heat and cold.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The star stays near the horizon, shaping a world without familiar sunrises.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Cities shelter beneath rock, supported by roots, pipes, food and managed light.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These conditions give the novel's arguments about limits a physical foundation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No leader can simply promise everyone more land beyond the next hill.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Before judging this civilization, the reader must understand what keeps it alive.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Nivari descend from creatures for whom a shadow could mean death.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their lateral eyes, mobile auditory sails and powerful limbs carry that history.
